_purpose: Identity of the site + samples that tests/e2e/ui-vs-export-parity.test.js drives on the live dev stack (GH-380). The harness switches the login user's active site to this site, generates the programme on /plan, exports exactly this soil sample from /reports/export, and asserts the two surfaces agree. It does NOT pin output numbers -- those come from the running code and must agree between surfaces, whatever they are.
_whyThisSample: Soil K sits BELOW the S277 floor (78.2 ppm), so the below-floor branch runs on every engine. Above the ceiling every engine returns 0 and a UI-vs-export divergence is structurally invisible -- the harness's one earlier 'successful' run (2026-09-07) was made at K=276 ppm and proved nothing about parity. The harness refuses to pass its precondition test unless every nutrient in mustBeBelowFloor is below the floor the Plan page resolved.
_source: docker exec gilba_mysql mysql -ugilba -pgilba_secret gilba: sites.id / samples.id=141 (soil, payload K 40 / P 40, edited 2026-09-08 22:38 UTC through the UI) / samples.id=144 (tissue, payload K 2 / P 0.62 / N 4.57, edited 2026-09-08 22:40 UTC through the UI) / site_configs(gaip).turf + nzDistributor, read 2026-09-09. If someone edits these samples again, update currentInputs here -- the harness fails its precondition test with the drift, not a fake parity failure.

soilSample._clientIdNote: sample-persistence.js: client_uid || payload.label || payload.sampleId || 'sample_' + id. Sample 141 has client_uid NULL and its payload carries only _label, so the client store keys it 'sample_141' and the export picker's checkbox is input[data-sample-uid='<siteId>::sample_141'].

crossSite._why: GH-389: per-site annual N in a multi-site Combined export was the headline fix of D31 stage 1 (GH-383) and was protected only by one manual run. Ticking a SECOND sample, from a different site with a different annual N target, is what makes the cross-site leak observable: before GH-383 every sample after the first inherited the active site's N target, because word-export.js read it from a hidden legacy input that nutrition-calendar.js's restoreFromPersisted() fills once and then refuses to refill. Burns' own target is 120 against Test5's 250, so a leak shows up as a wrong number rather than a coincidence.
